Latest news: Just a day after GPT-6 Astra's launch, it has begun rolling out to Business and Pro subscribers on the $100 and $200 monthly plans. This comes before the announcement of other new models, and is a step before the $20 Plus tier gets access.

It's just over a year since OpenAI unveiled the first GPT-5 series model. Now, GPT-6 Astra will bring upgrades to ChatGPT and Codex. Here's what you need to know.

GPT-6 Astra Details

OpenAI has officially introduced its new model, GPT-6 Astra, calling it "the smartest, most aligned model in the world."

Here's more of what was announced today:

OpenAI further explained how GPT-6 improves computer operation capabilities, allowing ChatGPT to control your Mac or other desktop computers, and even run in the background while you're working on other tasks:

OpenAI also said that GPT-6 Astra is "the most capable model for software engineering to date."

For Codex, GPT-6 also brings some new changes:

OpenAI called GPT-6 Astra "a major step forward in cybersecurity capabilities," noting that it has "reached a critical level of cybersecurity under our Preparedness Framework."

For this reason, the model will be rolled out to users slowly.

OpenAI stated: "GPT‑6 Astra begins rolling out today to a small group of organizations, and will be available to all ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Business, and Enterprise users in the coming days, as well as through the OpenAI API and AWS."

""Astra usage is included within existing subscription limits, and users and enterprises can purchase additional credits to increase usage. Pro, Business, and Enterprise plan users can also access GPT‑6 Astra Pro. Enterprise administrators can enable Astra for their workspace; it is not enabled by default at launch.""

GPT-6 Astra Background

GPT-5 launched on August 7, 2025, replacing GPT-4o and multiple reasoning models to become the default model in ChatGPT. Its standout feature is the automatic router: ChatGPT can quickly answer questions or engage in deeper reasoning depending on the query. OpenAI also claimed it makes fewer factual errors than GPT-4o.

Apple adopted this model in iOS 26, iPadOS 26, and macOS Tahoe 26. ChatGPT requests handled through Apple Intelligence—including Siri handoffs, Writing Tools, and Visual Intelligence—switched from GPT-4o to GPT-5.

GPT-5.1 brought warmer, more natural responses in November. December's "red alert" GPT-5.2 accelerated professional workflows in response to Gemini. GPT-5.3 Instant refined ChatGPT's "awkward" tone, and two days later GPT-5.4 Thinking debuted with a one-million-token context window and built-in computer operation capabilities.

OpenAI subsequently added GPT-5.4 mini and nano, the restricted GPT-5.4-Cyber, GPT-5.5 for higher autonomy, GPT-5.5 Instant, and the July GPT-5.6 Sol, Terra, and Luna models.

From Codex Mac App to New ChatGPT

The software surrounding these models also underwent transformation. In February, OpenAI launched a dedicated Codex Mac app as a hub for running multiple coding agents, reviewing changes, and scheduling tasks.

In July, Codex essentially replaced the original ChatGPT desktop app, combining chat, work, and Codex into one, while the old native client was renamed ChatGPT Classic.

For me, Codex is the single biggest change in how I use ChatGPT. I can outsource more work that doesn't require deep thinking, and even build tools I couldn't have created on my own on the Mac.

GPT-6 Availability

OpenAI said its brand-new GPT-6 model will initially only be available to members of its cybersecurity-focused Daybreak program. This mirrors the rollout pace of the previous-generation GPT-5.6 model.
